name.text: Types of Functions — identifying a function family from its graph (JSXGraph)

questiontext.text:
The graph of a function is shown below.

[[jsxgraph width="400px" height="320px"]] (function() { var scenario = {#scenario#}; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-5, 8, 5, -8], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); // 0 linear, 1 quadratic, 2 cubic with two turning points, 3 exponential var f, lo = -5, hi = 5; if (scenario === 0) { f = function(x){ return 0.5*x + 1; }; } else if (scenario === 1) { f = function(x){ return 0.4*x*x - 2; }; lo = -4.2; hi = 4.2; } else if (scenario === 2) { f = function(x){ return 0.15*x*x*x - 1.5*x; }; lo = -4.3; hi = 4.3; } else { f = function(x){ return Math.pow(2, x) - 3; }; hi = 3.5; } board.create('functiongraph', [f, lo, hi], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

What type of function does this graph most likely represent?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Each family of functions has a characteristic graph. A linear function \(y = mx + c\) has a straight-line graph, because its rate of change is constant. A quadratic function \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) has a U-shaped (or upside-down U-shaped) graph called a parabola, with exactly one turning point and a vertical line of symmetry. A cubic function \(y = ax^3 + \dots\) has an S-shaped graph with one point of inflection; it may have two turning points or none, and its two ends go in opposite directions. An exponential function \(y = a^x + k\) flattens out towards a horizontal asymptote on one side and becomes steeper and steeper on the other.

[[if test="is(scenario=0)"]]

The graph shown is a straight line, so the function is linear.

[[elif test="is(scenario=1)"]]

The graph shown is a parabola with one turning point and a vertical line of symmetry, so the function is quadratic.

[[elif test="is(scenario=2)"]]

The graph shown rises, falls, then rises again: two turning points, with its two ends going in opposite directions. So the function is cubic.

[[else]]

The graph shown flattens out towards a horizontal asymptote on the left and becomes steeper and steeper on the right, so the function is exponential.

[[/if]]

questiondescription.text: Grade 11 Functions 16.5 (Types of Functions). Identifies linear, quadratic, cubic, or exponential function families from the shape of a JSXGraph-plotted curve.

falsefeedback.text: Look again at the overall shape. Is it a straight line? How many turning points does it have, and is it symmetric about a vertical line? Does it flatten out towards a horizontal asymptote on one side?
